A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LGNSDE framework, with matching core equations and retained experiments. Their main text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original node-classification and leave-one-class-out OOD experiments on five graph datasets in Tables 1 and 3 and Figure 2.

after.justification: V4 retains original empirical results and adds noise-perturbation, active-learning, sensitivity, backbone, runtime, and broader OOD comparisons.

M1.justification: The prior/posterior SDE formulation, shared diffusion, variational objective, stochastic Runge-Kutta integration, and Monte Carlo prediction remain. Appendix C.1 adds an evaluated LGNSDE-GAT drift-backbone variant alongside the original GCN-based model, a limited architectural extension.

E1.justification: Both versions use Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, Amazon Computers, and Photo. V4 substantially expands task and input-condition coverage through active learning, classification with noisy test features, and feature-perturbation OOD detection; these are new scenarios on retained datasets.

E2.justification: V4 adds Graph GP to the standard-setting comparison, with completed results on Cora and Citeseer. Tables 13–14 introduce much broader OOD comparator sets, including GAT, GRAND, GREAD, MSP, ODIN, Mahalanobis, GNNsafe, GKDE, GPN, and GNSD. V1's comparisons contain GCN/GNN, GNODE, BGCN, and GCN ensembles.

E3.justification: V1 Table 2 specifies uniform hyperparameters, whereas v4 Tables 6–7 report validation-selected grid search. New experiments introduce test-only Gaussian noise scaled to feature variability, acquisition/retraining procedures, validation-selected thresholds for OOD accuracy, and additional AUPR/FPR95 metrics. The revised protocol description does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's entropy-distribution and label-leave-out analyses, v4 adds empirical noise robustness, random-versus-entropy acquisition comparisons, prior drift/diffusion sensitivity tests, GCN-versus-GAT backbone analysis, and runtime comparisons. These investigate robustness, uncertainty-guided selection, architectural dependence, and computational cost.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean ± standard deviation in their primary result tables. V4 newly specifies 20 weight initializations for fixed Planetoid splits and 100 random splits for other datasets; this discloses repetitions without establishing an increase. Its additional Tables 13–14 provide point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Standard-setting values are revised: LGNSDE's reported Cora AURC changes from 0.9968 in v1 Table 3 to 0.0702 in v4 Table 1, GNODE's Cora NaNs become finite results, and some AUROC/accuracy entries change. Original OOD AUROC/AURC values are retained. V4 adds extensive new outcomes, including broader comparisons where GNSD frequently leads. These are revised or newly reported results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V4 adds a semigroup existence theorem attributed to Lin et al. (2024) and makes Proposition 1 conditional on it, replacing v1's strong-solution statement with a mild-solution statement. It also revises the time and memory complexity claims substantially. The original Lipschitz/growth assumptions, variance inequality, perturbation bound, and most Appendix A proof steps remain.

C1.justification: The central contribution—Bayesian graph SDE uncertainty modeling with variance and stability guarantees—is retained. V4 extends its stated empirical contribution to noise robustness, active learning, and Graph GP comparisons. Its abstract and conclusion describe overall performance as competitive, tempering v1's general outperformance conclusion.

C2.justification: V4 newly interprets entropy acquisition as selecting informative labels and links noisy-input results to the perturbation bound. It adds explanations of solver-controlled depth, a short-time-horizon qualification of the exponential stability bound, and Graph GP memory limitations. This substantially expands v1's discussion of entropy separation and general computational concerns.

D1.justification: V1 provides a brief uniform-hyperparameter table. V4 adds search ranges for training budgets, weight decay, solver step size, and model dimensions; an early-stopping value of 20; dataset split and label-count tables; the noise-generation rule; and active-learning training details. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although selected configurations and runtime hardware remain unspecified.

R1.justification: V4 adds a dedicated related-work section distinguishing its approach from earlier graph SDE formulations, stochastic diffusion, Graph Posterior Networks, and belief-theory methods. It adds Graph GP and evaluation/dataset references, and changes the existence argument's attribution from Pham (2009) to Lin et al. (2024). This substantially develops the work's positioning.

P1.justification: V4 extensively expands and reorganizes the exposition through a separate GNODE background section, rewritten abstract and conclusion, revised theoretical narrative, dedicated related work, and more granular experimental and appendix sections. Much of the original method and proof prose remains, but the explanatory structure changes substantially.

P2.justification: The standard-results table moves from Appendix C into the main text and expands; the OOD table gains accuracy rows. Figure 1 gains a latent-state axis and revised caption, while Figure 2 is restyled. New active-learning curves, a backbone entropy display, and sensitivity, benchmark, runtime, and complexity tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical validation and sparse experimental documentation. Noise tests, random-versus-entropy active learning, sensitivity/backbone analyses, and broader OOD comparisons provide better evidence about the utility and limits of its uncertainty estimates; split, tuning, and repetition disclosures improve assessability. These gains are substantial despite unexplained AURC revisions, underspecified Appendix C.3 protocols, and an unclear connection between the newly invoked existence theorem and the proposed model.
